tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. Oct 6–21 items cover speculative-decoding security, knowledge-graph work, sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, and materials extraction.
whats_new: Oct 22 adds a spectral-intervention paper, an empirical KG-to-text benchmark, and a Bashkir parameter-efficient adaptation suite; none extends earlier items.
why_it_matters: Treat this as a reading list, not a thread: the useful items for platform engineers are the speculative-decoding attack surface and code-translation hallucination mitigations.

beats.headline: Speculative decoding and secure code generation get security-focused work
Knowledge graphs applied to observability and legal reasoning
Hallucinations in cross-language code translation, with mitigations
Search-state awareness for RAG agents, and LLM materials-data extraction
Spectral interventions, KG-to-text benchmarking and Bashkir adaptation land Oct 22

open_questions: Does the speculative-decoding defense add measurable latency over unprotected drafting?
Do the code-translation mitigations hold on languages outside the paper's test set?
Does independent replication confirm the spectral-intervention capability shifts?
take_for_builders: If you run speculative decoding in production, read the Oct 6 security paper and check whether your draft model is an untrusted input; skip the rest unless it matches your domain.
